translationRepairs: On the first day of the first month of spring in the sixth year of Xiansi, dingwei, the Emperor held audience in Chongyuan Hall to receive the New Year's felicitations, with the ceremonial guard arrayed according to regulation.

On the first day of the first month of spring in the sixth year of Xiande, dingwei, the Emperor held audience in Chongyuan Hall to receive the New Year's felicitations, with the ceremonial guard arrayed according to regulation.
Focus unit opens 顯德六年; 顯德 is the Later Zhou reign title Xiande. Xiansi is a false romanization, and replacing it with Xiande corrects the error without other wording changes.

(Institutional Compendium of the Five Dynasties: in the sixth year of Xiansi, an order to circuit governors declared that on each appointment or transfer a special edict is issued—what need for tally tokens? The requirement of bronze tally-fish should be abolished.)〉

(Institutional Compendium of the Five Dynasties: in the sixth year of Xiande, an order to circuit governors declared that on each appointment or transfer a special edict is issued—what need for tally tokens? The requirement of bronze tally-fish should be abolished.)〉
The annotation cites 顯德六年; that reign title is Xiande, not Xiansi. The proposed swap fixes only the romanization and leaves the rest of the note intact.

Zhang Yongde was then military commissioner of Cangzhou; having married a daughter of Taizu of Zhou, he alone was admitted to the sickroom by reason of kinship. The officials therefore spoke through Yongde: "The realm is not yet settled and the capital lies exposed; the regional lords all hope for upheaval in the capital.

Zhang Yongde was then military commissioner of Chanzhou; having married a daughter of Taizu of Zhou, he alone was admitted to the sickroom by reason of kinship. The officials therefore spoke through Yongde: "The realm is not yet settled and the capital lies exposed; the regional lords all hope for upheaval in the capital.
Focus unit has 澶州節度使; 澶州 is Chanzhou. Cangzhou would be 滄州, which the chapter uses separately (e.g. the halt at 滄州 before the northern campaign). The replacement corrects only that place name.
Zhang Yongde of Cangzhou, director of the palace front and imperial son-in-law, was relieved of his military posts and given acting grand marshal and concurrent grand councilor;
Zhang Yongde of Chanzhou, director of the palace front and imperial son-in-law, was relieved of his military posts and given acting grand marshal and concurrent grand councilor;
Focus unit begins 澶州節度使兼殿前都點檢; 澶州 is Chanzhou, not Cangzhou (滄州). The proposed wording restores the correct prefecture and preserves the rest of the sentence.

(Eastern Capital Epitome, Biography of Zhang Mei: Mei began as a petty clerk of the three departments and grain commissary at Cangzhou. While Shizong was stationed there, Mei met every request; after his enthronement, supplies never failed through years of campaigning—thanks to Mei.

(Eastern Capital Epitome, Biography of Zhang Mei: Mei began as a petty clerk of the three departments and grain commissary at Chanzhou. While Shizong was stationed there, Mei met every request; after his enthronement, supplies never failed through years of campaigning—thanks to Mei.
Focus unit places Zhang Mei as 澶州糧料使 and Shizong as 鎮澶州; both are Chanzhou. Rendering them as Cangzhou confuses 澶州 with 滄州; the proposal’s Chanzhou fix matches the Chinese.
Yet Shizong often recalled what had passed at Cangzhou and never treated him with full trust and favor.)〉
Yet Shizong often recalled what had passed at Chanzhou and never treated him with full trust and favor.)〉
Focus unit recalls 澶州所為; that place is Chanzhou, not Cangzhou. The single place-name correction aligns the English with the Chinese.
Cang and Bian are very near; if you do not return at once to steady men's hearts but linger here for fear of a day's travel, and the worst should befall—what of the imperial altars!"
Chan and Bian are very near; if you do not return at once to steady men's hearts but linger here for fear of a day's travel, and the worst should befall—what of the imperial altars!"
Focus unit has 今澶、汴相去甚邇; 澶 is Chanzhou (cf. 澶州節度使 / 澶淵 in the surrounding units), not Cangzhou. ‘Chan and Bian’ correctly shortens that pair in the same style as the faulty ‘Cang and Bian’.
On renchen, the army reached Qianning Army, and Wang Hong, the Northern Han-appointed prefect of Ningzhou, surrendered the city.
On renchen, the army reached Qianning Army, and Wang Hong, the Liao-appointed prefect of Ningzhou, surrendered the city.

Focus unit has only 偽寧州刺史, with no Northern Han label. The surrounding northern campaign (from 滄州 to 乾寧軍, then 益津關 and 瓦橋關) is the Liao/Khitan frontier drive of 959, so ‘Northern Han-appointed’ invents the wrong polity; ‘Liao-appointed’ restores the correct affiliation for this 偽 officer.
On guimao, the present sovereign reached Waqiao Pass first, and the Northern Han garrison commander Yao Neibin surrendered the city.
On guimao, the present sovereign reached Waqiao Pass first, and the Khitan garrison commander Yao Neibin surrendered the city.

Focus unit has 偽守將姚內斌 at 瓦橋關, again without a Northern Han label. Waqiao Pass belongs to the same Liao/Khitan Three Passes frontier as the rest of this northern campaign; ‘Northern Han garrison commander’ invents the wrong side, and ‘Khitan garrison commander’ corrects it.
